name: Sicilian Defense: Najdorf
description: The fighting answer to 1.e4: 1…c5 and the Najdorf's flexible 5…a6.

lines.name: English Attack (6.Be3)

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.9: …a6 is the Najdorf: it takes b5 from White's pieces and prepares …e5 or …b5.
notes.11: …e5 grabs space and kicks the d4 knight; d5 becomes the key square.
notes.13: …Be6 develops and controls d5, the hole White wants to use.

lines.summary: …a6, then …e5 and …Be6: control d5 and you control the Najdorf.

lines.name: English Attack, 9.Qd2

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.9: …a6 is the Najdorf: it takes b5 from White's pieces and prepares …e5 or …b5.
notes.11: …e5 grabs space and kicks the d4 knight; d5 becomes the key square.
notes.13: …Be6 develops and controls d5, the hole White wants to use.
notes.15: …Be7 gets ready to castle; White is preparing g4 and O-O-O.
notes.21: …b5 starts Black's own attack on the castled white king; it's a race.

lines.summary: Opposite-side castling means a race: White pushes g4-g5, Black answers with …b5-b4.

lines.name: 6.Be2

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.9: …a6 is the Najdorf: it takes b5 from White's pieces and prepares …e5 or …b5.
notes.11: …e5 against the quiet 6.Be2, the same reply as against 6.Be3.
notes.15: …O-O: next come …Be6, …Nbd7 and a fight for d5.

lines.summary: Same plan as against 6.Be3: …e5, develop, castle, and fight for d5.

lines.name: 6.Be2, 9.Be3

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.9: …a6 is the Najdorf: it takes b5 from White's pieces and prepares …e5 or …b5.
notes.11: …e5 against the quiet 6.Be2, the same reply as against 6.Be3.
notes.15: …O-O: next come …Be6, …Nbd7 and a fight for d5.
notes.17: …Be6 aims at d5, the key square in every …e5 Najdorf.

lines.summary: Quiet White play: develop with …Be6 and …Nbd7, then use the c-file and …b5.

lines.name: 6.Bg5

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.9: …a6 is the Najdorf: it takes b5 from White's pieces and prepares …e5 or …b5.
notes.11: …e6 here, not …e5: the pin on f6 makes d5 too weak after …e5.
notes.13: …Be7 breaks the pin on the f6 knight.
notes.17: …Nbd7 supports the f6 knight; next is …b5 and a queenside attack.

lines.summary: Against 6.Bg5, switch to …e6, unpin with …Be7, then …Qc7, …Nbd7 and …b5.

lines.name: 6.Bc4

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.9: …a6 is the Najdorf: it takes b5 from White's pieces and prepares …e5 or …b5.
notes.11: …e6 blunts the c4 bishop, which aims at f7.
notes.13: …b5 gains space and threatens …b4 against the c3 knight.
notes.17: …Qc7 guards e5 and avoids tricks on the a8 rook.

lines.summary: Block the c4 bishop with …e6, then expand with …b5; watch out for e5 tricks.

lines.name: Moscow (3.Bb5+)

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.5: …Bd7 blocks the check and offers to trade Black's lesser bishop.
notes.7: …Qxd7 recaptures and keeps the knight free to go to c6.
notes.13: …e6 prepares …Be7 and …d5 when White pushes d4.

lines.summary: Block with …Bd7, take back with the queen, and develop calmly; the trade helped Black.

lines.name: Alapin (2.c3)

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.3: …d5 hits e4 at once, before White can build a big centre with d4.
notes.5: …Qxd5 is safe because c3 takes the c3 square from White's knight.
notes.9: …Bg4 develops and pins the knight that defends d4.
notes.13: …Nc6 piles up on d4; Black is comfortable.

lines.summary: Meet 2.c3 with …d5: the queen recaptures safely, then …Nf6, …Bg4, …e6 and …Nc6 hit d4.

lines.name: Smith-Morra Gambit

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.5: …dxc3 accepts the pawn; Black must defend carefully but stays a pawn up.
notes.9: …d6 and …e6 make a solid wall against the c4 bishop.

lines.summary: Take the gambit pawn, build a …d6/…e6 wall, develop and castle; White's attack fades.

lines.name: 9.Rd1

notes.1: …c5 fights for d4 from the side, keeping the game unbalanced.
notes.5: …dxc3 accepts the pawn; Black must defend carefully but stays a pawn up.
notes.9: …d6 and …e6 make a solid wall against the c4 bishop.
notes.15: …Be7 prepares castling; the queen stays on d8 to cover d6.
notes.17: …e5 shuts the d-file and blunts White's pressure on d6.

lines.summary: Close the d-file with …e5, castle, and keep the extra pawn.
